questions.stem: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, which change most directly accelerates hepatic glycolysis at the rate-limiting step?
questions.explanation: Insulin raises F2,6BP (PFK-2 kinase active), the most potent PFK-1 activator. A: Citrate inhibits PFK-1. C: ATP inhibits PFK-1. D: G6P inhibits hexokinase, not PFK-1, and wouldn't accelerate glycolysis. E: Acetyl-CoA inhibits PDH, not PFK-1.

questions.stem: In untreated type 1 diabetes, reduced glucose uptake by which tissue contributes to the hyperglycemia?
questions.explanation: Insulin moves GLUT4 to the plasma membrane in skeletal muscle, adipose tissue and heart; without insulin these tissues take up little glucose. A: Erythrocytes use GLUT1, which is insulin-independent. B: Neurons use GLUT3, which is insulin-independent. D: Hepatocytes use bidirectional GLUT2, which is insulin-independent. E: Intestinal uptake uses the Na⁺-coupled SGLT.

questions.stem: During intense exercise, why does skeletal muscle convert pyruvate to lactate?

options.A: To make ATP at the lactate dehydrogenase step
options.B: To relieve ATP inhibition of PFK-1
options.C: To export glucose directly to the liver
options.D: To supply NADH to the respiratory chain
options.E: To regenerate NAD⁺ for glyceraldehyde 3-P dehydrogenase

questions.explanation: NADH production exceeds respiratory chain capacity; the high NADH/NAD⁺ ratio drives pyruvate → lactate, regenerating the limited NAD⁺ that glyceraldehyde 3-P dehydrogenase needs. A: LDH makes no ATP. B: Lactate doesn't regulate PFK-1. C: Lactate, not glucose, goes to the liver (Cori cycle). D: LDH consumes NADH; it doesn't supply it.

questions.stem: What is the net yield of anaerobic glycolysis (glucose → 2 lactate)?
questions.explanation: 4 ATP made − 2 invested = 2 ATP; NADH is reoxidized when pyruvate becomes lactate. B: 4 is gross, not net. C: Aerobic glycolysis to pyruvate nets 2 ATP + 2 NADH. D: Complete oxidation. E: There is a net gain.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with chronic alcohol use is confused and ataxic. He is given thiamine before glucose. Which enzyme requires the coenzyme form of thiamine (TPP)?
questions.explanation: PDH requires TPP (with lipoate, CoA, FAD, NAD⁺); giving glucose without thiamine can worsen Wernicke encephalopathy. A: LDH needs NADH only. B: Pyruvate carboxylase needs biotin. C: GAPDH needs NAD⁺. E: Pyruvate kinase needs no TPP.

questions.stem: A lean 16-year-old has mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia found on routine testing. Her father and grandfather have the same finding and have never needed insulin. An inactivating mutation in which enzyme is most likely?
questions.explanation: MODY2: glucokinase, the high-Km glucose sensor of hepatocytes and pancreatic β cells, is inactivated, giving mild fasting hyperglycemia. B: Low-Km hexokinase is saturated at normal glucose and can't act as a sensor. C: PFK-1 is the rate-limiting step of glycolysis, not the glucose sensor. D: Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes hemolytic anemia. E: Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency (von Gierke) causes fasting hypoglycemia.

questions.stem: An infant has seizures, developmental delay and microcephaly. CSF glucose is low while blood glucose is normal. A ketogenic diet improves the seizures. Which transporter is deficient?
questions.explanation: GLUT1 haploinsufficiency: glucose doesn't cross the blood–brain barrier in sufficient amounts; ketone bodies from a high-fat diet are an alternative brain fuel. A: GLUT2 serves liver and kidney. B: GLUT3 is neuronal, but the defect here is entry across the blood–brain barrier. D: GLUT4 is the insulin-regulated transporter of muscle, fat and heart. E: SGLT is Na⁺-coupled transport in the intestine, renal tubules and choroid plexus; its loss isn't the known cause of this syndrome.
